newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Quake rocks central Philippines, stirs mild panic.
newsitem.headline: Quake rocks central Philippines, stirs mild panic.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook the central Philippines on Wednesday, causing mild panic among residents, but there were no reports of casualties or damage, officials said.
Hundreds of people ran out of offices, restaurants and shops in the centre of Tacloban city when the tremor, measuring 6.2 on the Richter scale, struck at 5.48 p.m. (0948 GMT).

"It was quite strong. All of my staff, about 25 of us, ran out of the building. But all of us are safe," said Dalmacio Grafil, publisher of the Leyte-Samar Weekly Express newspaper in Tacloban, a city of about 200,000 people some 580 km (360 miles) southeast of Manila.
Government seismologists in Manila said the tremor originated in the sea 42 km (26 miles) northeast of coastal Borongan town on nearby Samar island. No damage was expected, they said.
It was the fourth earthquake in the Philippines in less than two weeks. The country is frequently hit by quakes but only a few are big enough to cause major damage.
